name: Inverse Finance Frontier
rootCause: Flashloan & Price Oracle Manipulation. Lost: 53.2445 WBTC and 99,976.29 USDT

descriptions.text: Flashloan & Price Oracle Manipulation. Lost: 53.2445 WBTC and 99,976.29 USDT
Flipped again. $1.2M to the anonymous attacker, and $5.8M lost overall. After two hacks in such quick succession, will Inverse be able to survive this crypto winter?

Incorrect LP price calculation via balanceOf. Vulnerable code snippet: https://etherscan.io/address/0xe8b3bc58774857732c6c1147bfc9b9e5fb6f427c#code#L120 Insecure way to calculation of LP price via balanceOf in the pool.

Inverse Finance suffered a flash loan attack, resulting in a loss of approximately 1068.215 ETH (approximately $1.26 million). This is the second time that Inverse Finance has suffered a flash loan attack in the past two months. The main reason for this attack is the use of insecure oracles to calculate LP prices.

Inverse Finance's Frontier money market on Ethereum was exploited via a flash-loan oracle manipulation on June 16, 2022. The attacker borrowed 27,000 wBTC, manipulated the Curve-based price oracle to inflate collateral value, and extracted about $1.2 million in wBTC and USDT. Most proceeds were converted to ETH and laundered via Tornado Cash. Inverse paused borrowing after the incident. Frontier relied on a manipulated Curve-based oracle (YVCrv3CryptoFeed) to price LP collateral. The attacker used a flash loan to distort pool balances, causing the oracle to overvalue their collateral. This enabled over-borrowing of DOLA, which was swapped for other assets and extracted.
